keyVerseText: And he put forth a parable to those which were bidden, when he marked how they chose out the chief rooms; saying unto them,
rootMeaning: The Greek verb ἐπέχω (epéchō) is derived from the preposition ἐπί (epí), meaning 'upon' or 'over,' combined with ἔχω (échō), meaning 'to have' or 'to hold.' Thus, its root sense conveys the idea of holding something upon or over something else, implying a sustained grasp or attention. This literal sense of 'holding upon' enriches the English glosses like 'take heed' or 'hold forth' by emphasizing an active, deliberate retention or focus rather than a passive glance or brief notice.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, ἐπέχω appears five times with a variety of English translations such as 'when he marked,' 'he gave heed,' 'stayed,' 'holding forth,' and 'take heed.' This range reveals its flexibility in conveying both physical and mental acts of holding or directing attention. It can mean to mark or observe carefully, to stay or remain, or to offer or hold out something. The consistency lies in the sense of intentionality—whether in observing, waiting, or presenting—highlighting a purposeful engagement.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, ἐπέχω invites believers to a posture of attentive engagement with God and His word. To 'take heed' or 'give heed' implies more than casual hearing; it calls for focused, sustained attention to divine truth and commands. This aligns with the Christian call to live thoughtfully and obediently, holding fast to the teachings of Christ amid distractions. Moreover, the idea of 'holding forth' suggests the active sharing or offering of spiritual truths to others, emphasizing the responsibility of believers to both receive and communicate God's life-giving word faithfully.
keyVerseReflection: In Luke 14:7, Jesus 'put forth a parable to those which were bidden, when he marked how they chose out the chief rooms.' Here, ἐπέχω conveys Jesus' careful observation of the guests' behavior. The word underscores His attentive awareness and purposeful reflection on their choices, setting the stage for the teaching that follows. It reminds readers that God notices our actions and attitudes, encouraging believers to live with humility and mindfulness before Him.
